newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA SIGNED FOR 30.3 MLN BBLS IRAQI OIL SO FAR.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA SIGNED FOR 30.3 MLN BBLS IRAQI OIL SO FAR.

text.p: Russian oil companies have so far signed up for 30.3 million barrels of Iraqi oil under the second U.N. oil-for-food programme, and more contracts are in the works, Interfax news agency said on Thursday.

It quoted Yuri Agababov, deputy director of Zarubezhneft, the Moscow-based firm coordinating all Russian purchases, as saying two more contracts of unspecified size could be signed in the future. Agababov was not available for comment.

Agababov was quoted as saying Zarubezhneft, LUKoil and Rosneft had each signed up for 5.5 million barrels. Zarubezhneft would lift from Ceyhan in Turkey, while the other two companies would unload both from Ceyhan and from Mina al-Bakr in the Gulf.

Alfa-Eko had increased its volume signed for in an earlier contract to 7.2 million barrels from 2.65 million. Tatneft would lift three million barrels, Nafta-Moskva 2.6 million and MES (International Economic Cooperation) one million. Those companies would lift from Mina al-Bakr. No other details were available.

Eight Russian companies lifted almost 28.54 million barrels under the first 180-day programme, or 23 percent of that total. With British companies more or less locked out of the second tranche, Russian companies are seeking to take an even bigger chunk.

The oil-for-food programme allows Baghdad to export around $2 billion in oil over six months to raise money to purchase food and medicine to alleviate the effects of U.N. sanctions imposed after Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1991.
